meta.title: Tic-Tac-Toe for Kindle & E-Ink — Free, No Download
meta.description: Play free Tic-Tac-Toe in your browser on Kindle, BOOX or Kobo. No download, no install — face an unbeatable AI or pass-and-play on one e-ink screen.

h1: Tic-Tac-Toe for Kindle & E-Ink — Free, No Download
tagline: Classic three-in-a-row that runs right in your Kindle Paperwhite, Scribe or BOOX browser — play an unbeatable computer or a friend on one screen, with nothing to download.

steps: Pick your opponent. Play against the computer, or switch to 2 Players and share one screen — X and O take turns on the same device, pass-and-play style.
Choose a difficulty. Easy still makes mistakes you can punish; Hard plays flawless minimax strategy and can never be beaten — the best anyone can do against it is force a draw.
Make a move. You always play X and move first. Tap or click any empty square on a touch screen, or press a number key: keys 1 through 9 map to the grid from top-left to bottom-right.
Navigate by keyboard. Arrow keys move a bold-framed cursor square by square; press Enter or Space to drop your piece on it. Backspace or U takes a move back.
Know the goal. Line up three of your marks in a row, a column or a diagonal. The winning line is flagged instantly with an inverted black-and-white highlight across its three squares.
Undo mistakes. Against the computer, one Undo steps back both your move and the computer's reply, returning the board to your turn; in two-player mode it takes back a single move.
Track the record. Your wins, losses and draws against the computer are counted on this device and shown beside the board — see how long you can hold a perfect opponent to a draw.

rows.note: The built-in browser runs the full game; needs firmware 5.13.7 or newer.
The 10.2-inch screen makes the nine squares huge and comfortable to tap one-handed.
Same browser engine as recent Paperwhites — the game stays black-and-white by design.

rows.device: BOOX (Go, Note, Tab, Palma and similar)
rows.note: Full Chromium browser, the smoothest e-ink experience; page-turn keys or a paired keyboard drive the cursor.
The built-in browser is dated and may not run the game on every model or firmware version.
No official browser app; third-party options require jailbreaking the tablet.
Pre-2016 experimental browsers can't run modern JavaScript — this page stays readable, but the game won't start.

whyEInk: Tic-tac-toe is nine squares and two marks, and e-ink redraws only the square you touch. No blinking, no animation, no refresh hiding behind the board — just crisp black strokes on paper-white. The grid reads perfectly in direct daylight and barely touches the battery, so a quick match never becomes a recharge break.

faq.a: Yes. Every game is free with no account, no paywall and no ads. The site belongs to the E-Ink.me family and is kept running alongside the free e-reader tools on the main site, so there is nothing to buy and nothing to sign up for.

faq.q: Does it work on my Kindle?
faq.a: If you have a Kindle from 2021 or later — Paperwhite, Scribe or Colorsoft — running firmware 5.13.7 or newer, yes. Open the built-in browser and load this page. Older Kindles with the early experimental browser can display this page as text, but the game itself will not start.

faq.q: Do I need to jailbreak my Kindle?
faq.a: No. The game runs entirely in the web browser your Kindle already ships with. There is no app to sideload and no hack to apply — if the device can open a web page, it can play. Nothing about your warranty changes.

You need an internet connection the first time this page loads, because the site is delivered as an ordinary web page rather than a downloadable app. Once loaded, the game runs on the device itself, and your board and win record are saved locally between visits.
